chunks: And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother Al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqteen who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who has intercourse with the virgin girl, neither ejaculating into her nor discharging upon her, is ritual bath obligatory upon her? And if she was not a virgin, then he had intercourse with her and did not ejaculate into her, is ritual bath obligatory upon her? He (peace be upon him) said: When the circumcised part touches the circumcised part, then the ritual bath becomes obligatory, whether she is a virgin or not.
ai.seo_question: When is a woman required to perform ghusl after intercourse if no ejaculation occurs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the specific physical criterion for obligatory ritual bath (ghusl) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that full penetration (where the circumcised part of the penis meets the circumcised part of the vagina) triggers the requirement regardless of ejaculation or virginity. This ruling distinguishes the Shia view from other schools by focusing on the anatomical connection rather than the emission of semen, ensuring ritual purity for subsequent prayers.

en.hubeali: And by this chain, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from his brother Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Yaqteen who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the man who overwhelms the virgin girl, neither deflowering her nor discharging upon her, would there be a washing upon her; and if she was not with virginity, then he overwhelms her and does not deflower her, would there be a washing upon her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the circumcised part falls upon the circumcised part, so the washing is Obligated, whether she was with the virginity or without the virginity’.
en.sarwar: 3. Through the same chain of narrators as that of the previous Hadith the narrator has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn from Ali ibn Yaqtin who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who pollutes a virgin girl who does not lose her virginity and does not discharge semen on her. Is Ghusl (bath) necessary on her or if she is not a virgin and he is exposed to her but intercourse does not take place, if Ghusl (bath) is obligatory on her? He (the Imam) said, ‘When private part falls on private part, Ghusl (bath) becomes necessary - virgin or not virgin.’”
